scene.note: The log is read one line at a time, and each step asks the one before it only for what it needs next.

steps.note: The winter's log is far too long to hold in memory at once.
Asked for a line, the reader takes one more line from the file and hands it over without its line end.
Between two asks it waits, holding only the line it last gave, and it closes the file after the last.
Lines come in one at a time.
A line goes on only when its call sign is the team's; a team named in another's message does not count.
Ailsa gets that team's calls one by one, and nothing is read ahead of what she asks for.
Lines come in one at a time, looking for a word.
Reading stops at the first line with the word in it.
Ailsa gets that line, or nothing at all when no line says the word.
The hours may come as a list or one at a time from a generator.
Both the largest and the total are worked out from the same hours.
Ailsa gets the two numbers together, whichever way the hours came.
